The 'name' GET parameter is concatenated directly into a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use '..' traversal sequences (e.g., ?name=../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files from the server.

User-supplied uploaded_file.name is concatenated into a shell command passed to os.system(). An attacker can craft a filename with shell metacharacters (e.g., '; rm -rf /') to achieve arbitrary command execution.

User-supplied uploaded_file.name is used to construct full_file_name via os.path.join. Because this filename later flows into os.system() in make_backup, a crafted filename with shell metacharacters results in command injection.
User-supplied 'user' POST parameter is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads(). Since pickle can execute arbitrary code during deserialization, an attacker can achieve Remote Code Execution.

The 'path' value is taken from request.POST without validation and used in HttpResponseRedirect(path). An attacker can craft a POST with path=http://evil.com to redirect users to a malicious site after login.

admin_update_user uses @user_is_authenticated but does not verify current_user.is_admin. Any authenticated non-admin user can update any user's email, password, first_name, last_name, is_admin, etc.
admin_get_all_users uses @user_is_authenticated but does not verify current_user.is_admin. Any authenticated non-admin user can retrieve the full list of all users.
